hero.title: Deconstruction of artichokes with cured ham
hero.subtitle: Auditing design systems in production
hero.description: On paper, our product's design looks like a Michelin-starred dish; but when it leaves the kitchen and reaches production, reality changes and the flavor is sometimes not what was expected.
recipe.title: The dish and its spec sheet
recipe.lead: To deconstruct is to separate the dish into its preparations and taste each one separately: does it taste like what its recipe promises?
recipe.adria: Ferran Adrià popularized deconstruction: separating the elements of a dish and serving them in a different way. We separate the website to taste each part.
recipe.sheetKicker: On paper · the spec sheet = your system
recipe.sheetTitle: Vega Baja artichokes with cured ham
recipe.sheetNote: Step 0 Ingredients = tokens, with origin and measurement.
recipe.ing5: Parsley, spearmint, oil, pepper, and salt
recipe.source: Recipe from the Asociación Alcachofa Vega Baja, prepared by Bodega La Venganza de Orihuela.
recipe.methodKicker: Leaving the kitchen · the served dish = your website
recipe.map:
• 1Step 1: Spoonfuls of brothBoil the bones until the liquid reduces by half and taste it by the spoonful.→ the sample and tokens in use
  • 2Step 2: PuréeCook four artichokes with parsley and blend them.→ the components
  • 3Step 3: Yolk and crumbsThe center of the dish and its flavor: sauté garlic and bacon; add the bread.→ the patterns and voice
  • 4Step 4: Low temperatureFour vacuum-sealed artichokes with spearmint, at 60 ºC for 30 minutes.→ the behavior
  • 5Step 5: PlatingPurée, yolk, crumbs, artichokes, and, finally, the broth.→ the diagnosis

s0.title: The system: tokens, assets, and guidelines
s0.metaphor: The recipe doesn't say «artichokes»: it says «Vega Baja artichokes». A good ingredient has an origin. A good token does too. Here the entire system is read, just once.
s0.cataElaboration: Each ingredient in the pantry: its file, its documentation, and its origin.
s0.cataHow: Where it is published, whether it is typed, and whether each semantic token points to a primitive.
s0.cataPoint: Each token has an origin, type, and measurement, and the documentation says the same thing as the file.
s0.prompt: «Before looking at the website, check the design system's pantry ([sistema]). Work with text: download the token files and read the guidelines as text, without screenshots or browser. Find where it publishes its tokens (ideally DTCG files). If there aren't any, look for them wherever the system defines them and indicate where each one comes from; if a piece of data is in a file and in the documentation, the file prevails. Review its two layers: the primitives (palette, font families, measurement scales, durations, and curves) and the semantics (decisions with intent: text, surface, border, focus, states…), checking whether each semantic token points to a primitive or repeats a hardcoded value. Also list the assets (logo, icons, illustration, photography, fonts) and the guidelines (components, patterns, voice, accessibility, motion). For each ingredient indicate its source, whether it is typed, whether there are duplicates or contradictions between documentation and file, and whether contrasts are measured. Do not look at the website yet. Save the result in audit/00-ingredients.md and create audit/board.md with the website, the system, what has been done, and what comes next.»
s0.test: Open the documentation and the token file yourself. Do you find what the AI says? Is anything missing that you would expect in the pantry?
s0.note: Ingredient · source · status (complete, incomplete, contradictory, or missing).
s1.eyebrow: I · Deconstruct · Step 1 · Spoonfuls of broth
s1.title: Sample, single capture, and token usage
s1.metaphor: To know if the stew has enough salt you don't eat the whole pot: you taste a few well-chosen spoonfuls and serve them in bowls, so you don't go back to the pot. And the broth, the tokens reduced to decisions: does it coat the whole dish or is it tap water?
s1.cataElaboration: Each page in the sample and each visible value: color, typography, spacing, radii, shadows, borders, durations, and curves.
s1.cataHow: You approve the sample; afterward, each page is captured once and each value is traced to its origin: semantic token, primitive, or hardcoded?
s1.cataPoint: The sample represents the website and everything visible comes from the system's semantic tokens.
s1.prompt: «We are going to audit [web] against its design system ([sistema]), with audit/00-ingredients.md. 1. Sample. Explore the website and propose a sample using WCAG-EM 2: the most common pages, one example of each type, complete processes, and an extra 10% at random. Propose it in three sizes so I can choose: the full one, which is the professional audit, or, so my AI uses less, the minimum (3 structured pages and 1 at random) or a single page. Draw the random pages in the browser using true randomness (crypto.getRandomValues) among the sitemap pages that are not in the structured sample and note how you drew it. Note people's main tasks and the processes that solve them. Save it in audit/01-spoonfuls-of-broth.md and stop: wait for me to confirm the sample. 2. Single capture. Once I confirm it, write an extraction script, save it in audit/tools/ and use it on each page of the sample, on desktop (1440 px) and mobile (360 px). Before measuring, have it request reduced motion, wait for the page to be stable, and not accept cookies. Have it write to audit/data/<page>/, without passing the data through the conversation: the screenshot (save it without opening it); the grouped computed styles (color, typography, radii, shadows, borders, durations, and curves, with how many elements use each value and whether it comes from a CSS variable, and for spacing only what is outside the system's scale); landmarks, headings, and controls with their names; the contrast of each text, images without alt text, touch targets smaller than 24 px, the Tab traversal (focus order and style), animations that continue with reduced motion, and horizontal overflow on mobile; and visible texts. Add a summary.md per page with only what is outside the system (at most 20 values per category, with their count). Before trusting the data, check on each page that it responded with status 200, that the screenshot is not obstructed, and that there are measured elements. 3. Broth. With the summaries and the tokens from 00-ingredients.md, tell me which values come from semantic tokens, from primitives used directly, or are hardcoded, which values do not exist in the system, which tokens are duplicated, and in which elements they appear. Calculate the percentage of each origin: this is the coverage that the report will use. Add the broth to audit/01-spoonfuls-of-broth.md and note in audit/board.md what has been done and what is next.»
s1.test:
Before saying «continue»: is any page missing that you would use? Add it. Did it note how it drew the random part?

Next, open a screenshot: is the full page visible? Inspect → Styles: does it say var(--…) or a literal value? Computed for the final value and CSS Overview for the whole page.

Without terminal: right-click on the element → Ask AI (DevTools AI assistance) → «Where do the color, typography, and animation duration of this element come from? Are they CSS variables or hardcoded values?»
s1.note: Declared sample (structured, random, and how it was drawn), tasks and processes; and each value with its origin (semantic, primitive, or hardcoded) and the token it should use.
s2.title: Components: anatomy, variants, and sizes
s2.metaphor: Blending the interface into pieces: how many versions of the same component exist and which ones come from the system?
s2.cataElaboration: Each piece of the interface: buttons, fields, cards, menus, icons…
s2.cataHow: Interface inventory: what should be the same component is grouped together and compared against its spec sheet in the system.
s2.cataPoint: Every component on the website exists in the system, with its variants documented.
s2.prompt: «With audit/data/ (read each page's summary.md first and the detail only if needed), create an interface inventory with these categories: global elements, navigation, images, icons, forms, buttons, headings, blocks, lists, interactive components, media, third-party, messages, colors, and animation. Group what should be the same component and compare it with its spec sheet in [sistema]: anatomy, variants, and sizes (states are reviewed later). Tell me what is on the website that does not exist in the system and which variants are undocumented, with page and element, and separate what the system does not cover (orphan: decided in governance) from what it defines and the website applies differently (fixed in the product). For each component, note a reference instance (page and selector). If you have doubts about something, crop only that element and save it in audit/screenshots/ with the step number and its name (for example, 02-boton-primario.png). Save the result in audit/02-puree.md and note in audit/board.md what has been done and what is next.»
s2.hint: Work from the step 1 capture, without opening the website.
s2.test: Put the screenshots side by side. Would a user notice?
s2.note: Component · variants found · system spec · orphan? · reference instance.
s3.eyebrow: I · Deconstruct · Step 3 · Yolk and crumbs
s3.title: Patterns, content, and voice
s3.metaphor: The yolk is the center of the dish: what people come to do. The crumbs give it flavor. Like breadcrumbs with egg, they are tasted together: is the task solved the same way everywhere and does it sound like the brand?
s3.cataElaboration: Each task people come to do, from start to finish, with its headlines, buttons, and messages.
s3.cataHow: Each task is walked through once, its pattern is compared with the one documented by the system, and each text is read alongside the voice guide.
s3.cataPoint: The same problem is solved the same way everywhere, sounds like the brand, and each thing is always called the same name.
s3.prompt: «With the tasks and processes from audit/01-spoonfuls-of-broth.md: 1. Yolk. Walk through each process in [web] once, up to validation and without submitting anything: do not click the final button of a form or accept anything that saves data. For each task, tell me which patterns it uses (navigation, form, confirmation, error, empty state, loading, consent…), whether the same problem is solved the same way everywhere, and whether [sistema] documents that pattern. Save the screenshot of the element in each error or confirmation state that appears in audit/screenshots/ with page, element, and state (for example, 03-contacto-email-error.png). 2. Crumbs. With the texts from audit/data/ and the messages that appeared during the walkthrough, review headlines, buttons, and messages against the voice guide of [sistema]: what complies, what does not comply, and which terms are used in different ways for the same thing. If the guide includes lists of words or expressions, search for them with a script instead of reading everything. Propose alternatives. Save the result in audit/03-yolk-and-crumbs.md and note in audit/board.md what has been done and what is next.»
s3.hint: The tasks already come from step 1; error and confirmation messages appear when walking through them.
s3.test: Do a task yourself from start to finish: where do you hesitate? Read its texts aloud: do they sound like the brand?
s3.note: Task · pattern · documented? · inconsistency. Current text · rule · alternative.
s4.title: Behavior: states, accessibility, and motion
s4.metaphor: 60 ºC for 30 minutes: what demands precision. Does it work for everyone, in all states and sizes?
s4.cataElaboration: Each state and each size, with mouse, with keyboard, and with reduced motion.
s4.cataHow: What is measurable (contrast, alt text, headings, keyboard, reduced motion, and mobile) comes from the capture; the states that must be interacted with, by opening the website.
s4.cataPoint: It works for everyone, in all states and sizes.
s4.prompt: «Review the behavior of the pages in audit/01-spoonfuls-of-broth.md against the specs and accessibility rules of [sistema]. Contrast, alt texts, headings, touch targets, Tab traversal, reduced motion, and mobile overflow are already measured in audit/data/: read them and do not measure them again. Error and confirmation states are already captured in step 3. Open [web] only for hover and active on the reference instance of each component from audit/02-puree.md, and for loading if a process has one. For each failure, save the screenshot of the element in that state in audit/screenshots/ with page, element, and state (for example, 04-home-boton-suscribirse-hover.png). Save the result in audit/04-low-temperature.md and note in audit/board.md what has been done and what is next.»
s4.hint: What is measurable is already in the capture; open the website only for what needs interaction.
s4.test: Press Tab from the beginning. Emulate reduced motion in Rendering, turn on responsive mode, and run Lighthouse → Accessibility.
s4.note: Rule or spec · where it fails · WCAG criterion if applicable.
s5.title: Diagnosis: report and system health
s5.metaphor: After deconstructing, it is plated again: each finding in its place and with its proof. This is what is served to the team to decide what to fix.
s5.cataElaboration: Everything tasted up to here, file by file.
s5.cataHow: Only what can be proven goes in, and the system is scored with the five criteria of the Michelin guide.
s5.cataPoint: Numbered findings, with screenshot and proposal, ready for the team to decide.
s5.prompt: «Download, without reading it, the report template (https://muirogles.github.io/deconstruccion-alcachofas/report-template.html) and save it as audit/05-report.html. Read the format of the sample data (https://muirogles.github.io/deconstruccion-alcachofas/findings-example.js), without saving it. Read files 00 to 04 in audit/ and remove from the findings anything you cannot prove, listing it with its type: false positive (you checked it and it is not a failure), to be verified (with what would be missing to prove it), or seen in passing (it belongs neither to the design system nor to accessibility; state who it should be passed to). If the same failure repeats on several pages, it is a single finding: use the most representative page, name the others in the impact and capture only that page. Number the remaining findings by impact: H-01, H-02, H-03… Write audit/findings.js with the same format as the example: summary, Michelin guide from 0 to 3 with evidence (the criteria and what each score means are in the example), system health (coverage, drift, duplicates, orphans, and parity), one card per finding (page, selector, state if not normal, layer, current value, system value, rule, impact, effort, proposal, and its screenshots (the width and alt text of each), all unverified: I will verify them), and the discarded ones. For each finding, save the screenshot of its element at each width from step 1 where it fails, with the width at the end of the name: audit/screenshots/H-01-1440.png, H-01-360.png…, opening each page only once per width and without looking at the screenshots; if steps 2, 3, or 4 already captured that element at that width, copy it with that name. Never reuse a name for two findings. Note in audit/board.md what has been done and what is next.»
s5.test: Open 05-report.html and pick a finding. Check it yourself: if it holds up, ask your AI to set its «verified» to true; if not, have it moved to discarded as a false positive, with the reason. Find at least one false positive.
s5.note: The report for your team: it renders on its own with findings.js, one card per finding with the screenshot of the specific element. It is in «Takeaway».
s6.title: Where it gets fixed and how it stays fixed
s6.metaphor: To adjust is to tweak little by little and taste each time; at the pass, the chef inspects every dish before it goes out. Is it fixed once in the system and does it keep tasting the same in every deployment?
s6.cataElaboration: Each finding from the report and each fix that reaches production.
s6.cataHow: In the recipe (system), once and for all screens; on the plate (product), with what the system offers; or on the menu (governance), proposing what is missing. Each criterion is re-checked only at the pass.
s6.cataPoint: Each adjustment has its criterion, is done in small rounds, and keeps tasting the same in every deployment: the system earns stars.
s6.prompt: «Read audit/findings.js. For each finding, decide where it is fixed: in the system, in the product, or in governance. Write one issue per finding, with its same number (H-01, H-02…) and link to its screenshots, with evidence, proposal, and an acceptance criterion written as a check that can be repeated without AI whenever possible (page, selector, expected value). Group those fixed with a single change in the system and order them into small rounds. Add to each finding in findings.js where it is fixed, its round, and its criterion. Save the issues in audit/06-adjust.md and note in audit/board.md what has been done and what is next.»
s6.hint: A human decides; the AI only proposes. The pass is done by the kitchen: the automated pass, in «Takeaway».
s6.test: Is the place where it gets fixed well chosen? Fixing in the system fixes all screens; fixing on one screen fixes nothing else.
s6.note: Finding · where it gets fixed · proposal · acceptance criterion · round.
michelin.eyebrow: II · Plate · Does it deserve the star?
michelin.title: The system's Michelin guide
michelin.lead: Its 5 official criteria, translated to the system. Each one is scored from 0 to 3, with its evidence.
michelin.caption: Official criteria and their translation
michelin.criteria:
• 1Quality of ingredientsTokens and assets with a single source, typed, and with origin.Steps 0 · 1
  • 2Mastery of techniquesComponents faithful to their specs, accessible, and with all their states.Steps 2 · 4
  • 3Harmony of flavorsThe same problem, solved the same way everywhere.Steps 1 · 3
  • 4Personality of the chef expressed in their cuisineThe brand is recognizable without seeing the logo.Steps 0 · 3
  • 5Consistency across the entire menu and over timeAcross the entire sample and from one audit to the next.Steps 1 · 6
michelin.starsList:
• ★One star: worth a stop
  • ★★Two stars: worth a detour
  • ★★★Three stars: worth a special journey
michelin.starsNote: A metaphor to prioritize and communicate.
tools.title: What accompanies the recipe
tools.lead: Choose whatever you have on hand: they all pair with the recipe. And the gran reserva, for the dishes that call for it.
tools.manual: Chrome or Edge: Computed, CSS Overview, Rendering (reduced motion), and Lighthouse. Firefox: accessibility inspector, with contrast and color vision. Safari: Web Inspector. And the Tab key.
tools.noTerminal: Chrome: right-click on an element → Ask AI and it explains its styles. Edge (experimental): Copilot explains console errors with Explain this error. Useful for checking a specific finding, not for auditing the whole page.
tools.mobile: No files: paste the result from the previous step into the chat and launch the next one. Works for judgment steps (2, 3, 5, and 6); exact values (step 1 and contrast in 4), on desktop. Note everything down on the tasting sheet.
tools.agent: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or Gemini CLI with Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, agent-browser, or the VS Code browser. Have it browse, test mobile and desktop, read the accessibility tree, measure styles, and save screenshots.
house.title: Who cooks what
house.lead: The AI writes the recipe once and the kitchen repeats it at no cost. In each course: what repeats on its own, what your AI proposes, and what you decide.
incognito.title: We dine incognito
incognito.lead: Michelin guide inspectors book under another name, pay the bill, and behave like any customer: that way they experience the exact same thing as their readers.
incognito.list:
• What reaches the table. We audit the website in production, the one people experience.
  • Without entering the kitchen. No repository or special access: a browser and your AI.
  • Anyone can repeat it. Your team, the public, or you tomorrow.
practice.scopeText: Live, only the home page on desktop and mobile. In the challenge, minimum 3 pages + 1 at random. In your audit, the sample you approve in step 1.
practice.scopeNote: If there is no time, pre-cook some steps beforehand with these same orders and mark them as served on the rail.
service.title: Cooking with Arcasiles
service.lead: The same recipe, now on a real website. First, the table. Then, each order in its sequence: fire it, check what comes out, and mark it as served.
service.tableText: Enter your website and your system: all orders on the rail fill themselves in. They are saved only in your browser.
service.scopeText: Only for this demo and for time: limit the sample to the home page (on desktop and mobile). In a real audit, use the full sample.
service.preset: Put Arcasiles URLs in all orders
service.resetHelp: «New table» clears the website, the system, and the status of all orders.
service.railHelp: «Fire and copy» sends it to your AI. You click «Mark as served» once its file is saved.
service.courseAll: Full menu · courses I to III
service.msgReset: New table: website, system, and orders cleared
service.pickup: Pick up: every time the website changes.
challenge.title: Now you cook
challenge.lead: Audit the Arcasiles website with the complete recipe, from order No. 00 to No. 06, and find the secret ingredient.
challenge.sample: Minimum sample: 3 structured pages + 1 random, so your AI uses less. The professional choice is the full sample it proposes in step 1. No maximum: the more, the better.
challenge.text: Arcasiles will announce the rules, the deadline, the prize
challenge.closing: Deconstructing is not breaking the dish: it is understanding it piece by piece.

takeaway.slowPrompt: «Audit [web] against its design system ([sistema]). Save each step in its file inside audit/ and note in audit/board.md what has been done and what comes next: 0. Ingredients: read as text, without a browser, the primitive and semantic tokens (DTCG files if they exist; otherwise, wherever the system defines them), the assets, and the guidelines, with their source, types, duplicates, and contradictions → 00-ingredients.md. 1. Spoonfuls of broth: propose a sample with WCAG-EM 2 (common pages, one example of each type, complete processes, and an extra 10% drawn in the browser with crypto.getRandomValues among the sitemap pages) in three sizes so I can choose: the full one, which is the professional audit, or, so my AI uses less, the minimum (3 structured pages and 1 at random) or a single page; note tasks and processes, and stop until I confirm the sample. Then write in tools/ an extraction script that captures each page on desktop and mobile, with the page stable and reduced motion, without passing data through the conversation: screenshot, grouped styles with their count and origin, accessibility, Tab traversal, texts, and a summary.md per page with what is outside the system. Tell me what comes from semantic tokens, from primitives, or is hardcoded, and at what percentage → 01-spoonfuls-of-broth.md. 2. Purée: with the summaries, component inventory (anatomy, variants, and sizes) against their specs, separating orphans from implementation differences, with a reference instance of each → 02-puree.md. 3. Yolk and crumbs: walk through each process once, up to validation and without submitting anything; patterns for each task and voice of headlines, buttons, and messages against the guide → 03-yolk-and-crumbs.md. 4. Low temperature: read what is already measured; open the website only for hover and active of each component and for loading; capture each failure in its state → 04-low-temperature.md. 5. Plating: remove from the findings anything you cannot prove, with its type (false positive, to be verified, or seen in passing); a failure that repeats on several pages is a single finding, with the most representative page; number the findings H-01, H-02… by impact; write findings.js with the format of https://muirogles.github.io/deconstruccion-alcachofas/findings-example.js; save the screenshot of each finding's element at each width where it fails (screenshots/H-01-1440.png, H-01-360.png…; never the same name for two findings) and download, without reading it, the template https://muirogles.github.io/deconstruccion-alcachofas/report-template.html as 05-report.html. 6. Adjust: for each finding, where it gets fixed (system, product, or governance), an issue with an acceptance criterion that can be checked without AI, and its round → 06-adjust.md and findings.js. Anything you cannot prove leaves the findings, with its type; everything else remains "sin verificar": I will verify it. Apart from the sample, do not ask me anything until you finish.»
takeaway.slowHint: Confirm the sample, go get a coffee, and plate when you return: the agent works in the meantime.
takeaway.filesLead: If it stays in the chat, it's lost. Each step leaves its file and the next one reads it: your AI repeats nothing and spends less. Each course, a new table: a clean session that starts by reading board.md.
takeaway.treeTip: Each major change, a folder with the date: start from the previous report, audit only what is new, and compare the stars.
takeaway.reportText: The plating from step 5: your AI writes the findings and the report renders on its own, with one card and its screenshot per finding. To share it: Print → Save as PDF.
takeaway.templateText: To jot down by hand, from mobile or from a chat. The same steps, in a single file that is easy to send.
board.duty: Golden rule: your AI cooks, but you taste the dish. The responsibility remains yours.
board.label: From the house
board.caption: Who cooks what in each course
board.thead: Who I · Deconstruct II · Plate III · Adjust and pass
board.tbody: Without AI scripts and DevTools the report renders on its own the automated pass Your AI relates and groups drafts and prioritizes drafts issues You approve the sample, walk through, and check look for false positives decide where it gets fixed
automate.title: Automate the pass
automate.windowLead: Ask for the automated pass: first, a check without AI; AI, only when judgment is needed.
automate.gatePrompt: «With what is in audit/, prepare what is needed to repeat the audit of [web] without starting from scratch. First, what works without AI; AI, only for what requires judgment: 1. A check without AI, that always gives the same result: have it reuse the extractor from audit/tools/, compare the website's values with the tokens from 00-ingredients.md and flag those that are hardcoded, and repeat the acceptance criteria from findings.js to confirm that already fixed findings (H-01, H-02…) are still good. Explain how to run it depending on what I have: in the browser, on my computer, or in the repository after each deployment. 2. A skill (SKILL.md, or reusable instructions depending on my tool) with the recipe in two phases: first that check, at no cost; then, AI only for what requires judgment, such as task patterns and voice (step 3) or reviewing in the screenshots the visual changes flagged by the check. 3. If it makes sense, an agent (auditor-agent.md) that runs the check first, turns to AI only if it finds something the check cannot judge, and leaves the final decision to me. Each time it runs, have it save the new screenshot of each finding as screenshots/H-01-1440-pass.png, screenshots/H-01-360-pass.png… (at each width of its screenshots) and note with the date whether it meets its criterion, whether it broke anything else, and how health and the stars stand. Save everything in audit/automated-pass/ and explain in audit/automated-pass/how-to-use.md, in plain language, what each piece is for and how to use it.»
automate.gateHint: Start with what you can run today with what you already have.
